propers.name: Collect
propers.text:
Domine Jesu Christe, qui, Mariae et Joseph subditus, domesticam vitam
ineffabilibus virtutibus consecrasti: fac nos, utriusque auxilio, Familiae
sanctae tuae exemplis instrui; et consortium consequi sempiternum: Qui vivis
et regnas cum Deo Patre in unitate.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n179, printed p. 179, under `Prayer` in the Mass of the Holy Family. The facing Latin is the 1962 slot's prayer outside pointing and the abbreviated conclusion; nothing is supplied from the excluded inserts.
translations.source_label: The New Roman Missal in Latin and English, revised edition, by F. X. Lasance and Francis Augustine Walsh (New York: Benziger Brothers, 1945), ca. 1955-56 printing (Internet Archive delivery locator fr-lasance-missal-1937; locator mislabelled)
translations.text: O Lord Jesus Christ, Who, in the days of Thy subjection to Mary and Joseph, didst consecrate home life by ineffable acts of virtue; by the intercession of Thy holy Mother and of Thy foster-Father, make us so to profit by the example they with Thee have set us, that we may be counted members of Thy household for evermore. Who livest.

propers.name: Secret
propers.text:
Placationis hostiam offerimus tibi, Domine, suppliciter deprecantes: ut, per
intercessionem Deiparae Virginis cum beato Joseph, familias nostras in pace
et gratia tua firmiter constituas. Per eundem Dominum nostrum Jesum
Christum, Filium tuum: Qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitate.

translations.caution:
A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Leaf n181, printed p. 181, under `Secret`. The facing Latin retains `deprecantes` before `ut`, and the English visibly renders that retained word as `humbly beseeching Thee that`; the rest is the 1962 slot's prayer outside pointing and the abbreviated conclusion.
translations.source_label: The New Roman Missal in Latin and English, revised edition, by F. X. Lasance and Francis Augustine Walsh (New York: Benziger Brothers, 1945), ca. 1955-56 printing (Internet Archive delivery locator fr-lasance-missal-1937; locator mislabelled)
translations.text: To appease Thee, O Lord, we offer the Victim of Salvation, humbly beseeching Thee that, through the prayers of the Virgin Mother of God and of St. Joseph, Thou wouldst establish our households in Thy peace and favor. Through the same.

propers.name: Postcommunion
propers.text:
Quos caelestibus reficis sacramentis, fac, Domine Jesu, sanctae Familiae
tuae exempla jugiter imitari: ut, in hora mortis nostrae, occurrente
gloriosa Virgine Matre tua cum beato Joseph; per te in aeterna tabernacula
recipi mereamur: Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre in unitate.

A lay hand missal of the 1945 revision, printed about 1955-56, not an approved liturgical translation and never an altar book. Its Holy Week is the pre-1955 rite, its sanctoral is not the 1962 sanctoral, and its second and third orations are not those of 1962. It is carried only where a 1962 formulary is the same prayer, and nothing here may be used for recitation.

Begins on leaf n181, printed p. 181, and finishes on leaf n182, printed p. 182; both leaves were opened. The facing Latin is the 1962 slot's prayer outside pointing and the abbreviated conclusion.
translations.source_label: The New Roman Missal in Latin and English, revised edition, by F. X. Lasance and Francis Augustine Walsh (New York: Benziger Brothers, 1945), ca. 1955-56 printing (Internet Archive delivery locator fr-lasance-missal-1937; locator mislabelled)
translations.text: Do Thou, O Lord, bring us whom Thou hast refreshed with heavenly mysteries to imitate the example of Thy holy Family, that at the hour of our death, with the Virgin Mother and blessed Joseph at hand, we may be received by Thee into our everlasting home. Who livest.
